_description: Starter concept config for GR-Neutro (7-class multi-label neutrophil abnormality task). Two options are supported: (A) classes-as-concepts — the 7 labels are used directly and the constraint penalty operates on the sigmoid outputs of the 7-way classifier; this is the minimal-change path from the MIDL 2025 codebase. (B) decomposed concepts — the 7 classes are re-expressed as compositions over a smaller set of low-level morphological features, and the CBM adapter predicts those features. Start with option (A). Option (B) is laid out as a TODO for the next iteration.

_option_A_classes_as_concepts.note: Simplest entry point. Each class IS a concept. Use these arrays directly with the methodology in aml_matek/ by setting num_concepts = num_classes and concept_targets = class_targets (already one-hot / multi-hot from the dataset).

_option_B_decomposed_concepts_TODO.note: Not implemented yet. The idea is to break each of the 7 classes into low-level morphological features that transfer across classes. This gives the adapter a tighter bottleneck AND moves the constraint closer to physical biology.
_option_B_decomposed_concepts_TODO.class_to_low_level_matrix_TODO: Fill in once a hematologist signs off on the decomposition. The translations are: Normal = round/3-lobed nucleus + normal granule count + no inclusions. Chromatin = coarsely clumped chromatin. Dohle = basophilic inclusion body. Hypergranulation = granule_count_above_normal + granules_present_toxic_dark. Hypersegmentation = nucleus_5_or_more_lobes. Hypogranulation = granule_count_below_normal + cytoplasm_pale_washed. Hyposegmentation = nucleus_2_lobes + nucleus_unsegmented_band.
_option_B_decomposed_concepts_TODO.why_bother_with_option_B: In AML Matek, option-A-equivalent (classes-as-concepts) showed that mutex constraints barely matter because the 15-way softmax already forces single-winner predictions. In GR-Neutro option-A the task is multi-label so mutex constraints already matter more — this is why this starter config leads with option A. But a decomposition also lets the model share statistical strength across classes that use the same low-level feature (e.g. the nucleus-lobes feature is used by both Hypersegmentation and Hyposegmentation with opposite signs), which is typically where CBMs really pay off. See docs/concept_design.md §5.
